lines.text: Diagnosis

elements.text: Diagnosis

lines.text: This variety is distinct from all other known
varieties in having the following combination of
characters: a light green colour, medium width
leaves, amedium-erect post-heading growth habit
and fewer spikelets per spike.

lines.text: Comparative Growing Trials

elements.text: Comparative Growing Trials

lines.text: All characteristics described and comparisons are
from comparative growing trials conducted at
Courtenay (near Christchurch) in the Canterbury
district, on the South Island of New Zealand in the
1982/83 and 1983/84 seasons. In 1982, 100 plants,
each with 3 cloned replicates was used ina
randomised block pattern of spaced plants with 60
cm spacing. In 1983, 200 plants with replicates
were used in a randomised complete block design
with 60 cm between blocks and 1 m between rows.
Further trials, to assess for field tolerance to the
diseases net blotch (Drechs/era dictyoides f.sp.
perenne) and crown rust (Puccinia coronata), were
conducted at Hamilton, in Victoria, Australia in

elements.text: Origin

lines.text: This variety arises from the open crossing of four
parent lines and is sustained through generations

elements.text:
This variety arises from the open crossing of four
parent lines and is sustained through generations

lines.text: by open crossing of the progeny. The parent lines
were selected from the polycross progeny testing
of 154 lines from 1975 to 1978 at two sites in the
Auckland district on North Island, New Zealand.
The main criteria for selection were vegetative
yield and crown rust (Puccinia coronata) resistance
of their progeny. The four parent lines all
originated at Mangere in Auckland district.

‘Yatsyn 1‘ is a semi-erect medium-green variety.
Most of the distinguishing or stable characteristics
are presented in the comparison tables. Those
recorded but not included are:

lines.text: degree of aftermath heading which is about the
same as ‘Ellett’;

lines.text: tiller density at heading which is higher than ‘Ellett’

lines.text: stem length which is shorter than ‘Grasslands Nui’;
a high proportion (the same as ‘Ellett’) of immature
leaves being foided in shoots rather than rolled;
and small leaf auricles.
Other characteristics were recorded but found to be
unstable. These include the number of leaf nodes
per stem, flag leaf inclination and anthocyanin
pigmentation.
